### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **80** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via keyId (symbol, a field of class RedactionAmender))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class), armSealer (symbol, a field of interface AuditPluginOptions), cryptoProvider (symbol, a field of interface AuditPluginOptions))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via byObject (symbol, a field of interface KeyMaterialMigrationReport; a field of interface MailLogBodyMigrationReport; a field of interface StoredMetadataBodyMigrationReport), sys_audit_amendment (symbol, a field of const object arObjects; a field of const object deObjects; a field of const object enObjects; a field of const object esESObjects; a field of const object frObjects; a field of const object jaJPObjects; a field of const object koObjects; a field of const object ptBRObjects; a field of const object ruObjects; a field of const object zhCNObjects; a field of const object zhHantObjects), os migrate audit-key-material (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-key-material.ts), os migrate audit-mail-bodies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-mail-bodies.ts), os migrate audit-metadata-bodies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-metadata-bodies.ts), os migrate stored-references bind (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-references/bind.ts))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/push-service.mdx`  _(via keyId (symbol, a field of class RedactionAmender))_
- `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class), AuditPluginOptions (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via os migrate stored-references bind (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-references/bind.ts))_
- `content/docs/plugins/index.mdx`  _(via keyId (symbol, a field of class RedactionAmender))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via os migrate audit-metadata-bodies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-metadata-bodies.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via os migrate audit-metadata-bodies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-metadata-bodies.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 49 pages)`
- **28** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `917ea0aace2cbace533bd99be203d0fdbc647b74` — the merge of head `2c47c2856324541e38c8404ad41ad25b44d00b29` into base `cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 917ea0aace2cbace533bd99be203d0fdbc647b74 && git checkout 917ea0aace2cbace533bd99be203d0fdbc647b74
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b 2c47c2856324541e38c8404ad41ad25b44d00b29 && git checkout -B drift-repro cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b && git merge --no-ff 2c47c2856324541e38c8404ad41ad25b44d00b29

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `06ca6d0db09b79e21c2d4cc8787cccc5a0ebe0ee`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

What holds, measured by an independent reviewer at the ceiling tier and adopted by the seat:
- D7 order: the amendment is written before the rewrite.
- A failed amendment write refuses the row, leaves it untouched, and counts it as `refused`; the CLI exits 1.
- An unsealed row is rewritten with no amendment.
- The amendment carries every field D7 lists, with the checkpoint's own salt, and is signed.
- The dry run decides alike and writes nothing.
- The verifier accepts what the writer writes on the honest paths.
- S9: `os serve` passes the host provider from inside the auth-gated block, above the stack `plugins` loop (both positions still pinned). It is read at `kernel:ready`, and the `requires: ['audit']` branch gets the same provider. Every one-shot `AuditPlugin` in the CLI passes `armSealer: false`.

What does not hold:
- **must-fix · F1, F2, F3 (audit integrity).** Before the redaction writer proves a row or decides an amendment is already written, it must admit every stored input it reads (prior amendments and the checkpoint body with its leaf list) only if that input verifies under a key D6's rule trusts. That is the same admission the verifier applies. A row the writer cannot prove against trusted, signed inputs is refused, never amended. This needs pins that bind the rule: an input that does not verify is never admitted, and the row stays refused.
- **should-fix · F5.** The writer must find a sealed row's checkpoint by an identity that a later change to the row cannot move. A sealed row whose checkpoint it cannot find is refused, not rewritten.
- **should-fix · F8.** `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1 os serve` is a one-shot boot that now arms the sealer with the host provider and runs a pass at once. Decide it (keep the sealer off, per seat ruling 6795974647 (a)) and pin it. The current pin excludes `serve.ts`.
- **should-fix · F4.** The `os migrate audit-*` docs must tell the operator to run these with the server stopped (the seat's ruling on open question 4). The sealer-lock fix is owed with P4.

### ② Semver level

The widening faces: `AuditPluginOptions.armSealer`, a function-valued `cryptoProvider`, `seal?` on the three migrations, `refused` on their reports, and a registered `sys_audit_amendment`. The `os migrate audit-*` JSON gains `refused`, and the commands exit 1 when they refuse a row. No previously accepted call is refused. The declaration is `Clause-②: yes (widening)` + `Metadata-protocol: none` + `patch`, with no `(narrowing)` arm owed. The head as reviewed still read `Clause-②: no` (F11); the dev's patch round corrects the changeset, and the seat corrects the PR body.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Audit tamper-evidence is a security boundary. F1–F3 are the must-fix class above; they are stated here at the rule level only.
- Not relaxed: no provider, an unopenable seed, a signer that throws, a key-id mismatch, an amendment insert that fails, and a column sealed in clear each refuse the row. Logging levels hold (`warn` plus a non-zero exit plus a closing error).
- #9863: the one option now passed is the host's own provider, not a config-derived helper. The pin's other assertions are unchanged, so this is read as inside that seat ruling, and the seat records the confirmation here.
- PR author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` through the relay.

### ④ Design judgment

- The decide / prove / write split and proving the leaf before signing are the right shape. The gap is unauthenticated inputs, which is one shared "trusted keys" step closing F1–F3, and it belongs in this slice.
- Owed before P4 seals `sys_audit_log` by default: the sealer/migration lock (F4); the ruling on an app-supplied `AuditPlugin` that supersedes the host's; `@objectstack/verify`'s `bootStack` mounting the plugin crypto-less; the stale `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['plugin-audit']` comment in `packages/spec`.
- Nits, taken as accepted deviations: a malformed checkpoint holds nothing, which matches the verifier; `seal` stays optional, per the seat's ruling on OQ5; one checkpoint-count assertion in `verify.integration.test.ts` cannot fail on its own, since the stderr assertion beside it discriminates; the live suite's cases depend on their order; the local-signer fallback on a one-shot boot is a stage-2 concern.

Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcSZ51q2s3nMfakhdJ3`

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `150cac4bdd06dfefedde11ace96593e358a57b34`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

A full re-review of the round-2 head by an isolated reviewer, adopted by the seat. Face: the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone. The committed tree touches no `packages/spec/src/**` file and no governed path (52 files, `record-recognisers --paths` decides no face).

Each finding of record 6820203096, read in the diff at this head:

- **F1, F2, F3 (must-fix): closed.** The redaction writer admits a stored checkpoint, and a stored redaction amendment, only when its signature verifies under a key the trust anchor vouches for. The rule is the verifier's own: `SigningKeyTrust` and `anchoredPublicKeyOf` moved out of `VerdictLedger` in `verifier.ts`, and both the live check and the writer call them, so there is one D6 rule and not two. A row that a non-verifying checkpoint lists is refused. A non-verifying amendment is neither proof for a row nor a reason to skip the amendment a rewrite owes. The checkpoint's leaf list is admitted only after it rebuilds the signed root. Four rule-named pins in `audit-seal-redaction-live.integration.test.ts` bind this; the dev report names the ablation that turns each red.
- **F5 (should-fix): closed.** A row's checkpoints are found by the row ids they list, never by the row's own `created_at` or `tenant_id`. A sealed row whose `created_at` moved is refused (pinned).
- **F8 (should-fix): closed.** `os serve` reads `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT` once, ahead of both `AuditPlugin` constructions, and both pass `armSealer: !migrateAndExit`. The exit reads the same constant. The contract test pins the one reading, its position, and both constructions.
- **F4 (should-fix): closed.** `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` says to run the `os migrate audit-*` commands with the server stopped, and why. The lock stays owed with P4, as ruled.
- **F11 (the declaration): closed in the changeset**, which carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The PR body still reads `Clause-②: no`; correcting it is the seat's, before ready.

What holds on the whole diff:

- S9: `os serve` hands the auth-gated `AuditPlugin` the host provider as a function read at `kernel:ready`, and the `requires: ['audit']` branch the same provider. The four one-shot constructions in the CLI (`data-migration-plugins.ts`, `schema-migration-plugins.ts`, `plugin-trust-store.ts`, `stored-references/bind.ts`) pass `armSealer: false`, and a package-wide source pin names any new one that forgets it.
- P3, D7 order: decide, then sign and store the amendment, then rewrite. A failed amendment write leaves the row as it is and counts it `refused`. An unsealed row is rewritten with no amendment. The dry run decides the same way and writes nothing. A second redaction names the commitment the checkpoint sealed. The three migrations and both stores (hot, archive) go through the one writer, and each CLI command exits 1 on a refused row.
- Head check-runs: 58 in all, 39 `success`, 19 `skipped`, none failed or pending. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (8 shards), `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are among the green.

No must-fix and no should-fix at this head. Nits, none of which touch correctness or the contract:

- **N1.** In the `requires: ['audit']` branch the one-shot posture is passed only when the host provider was built. When the settings package does not load, a migrate-and-exit boot mounts the plugin with its sealer armed and no provider: it logs the unsealed-objects error and writes nothing. Accepted deviation.
- **N2.** The writer re-verifies a checkpoint's signature, rebuilds its root and opens its seed once per row it lists, so a large window costs time quadratic in its row count. A follow-up card under #31908, before P4 seals `sys_audit_log` by default: admit and open each checkpoint once per run.
- **N3.** PR body prose is stale against the head (the test count, the head its verification block names, the refusal causes of round 2). Prose only; the seat's body edit covers it.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/cli`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and no `(narrowing)` arm owed. What widens, all covered by the declaration and named in the changeset:

- `AuditPluginOptions.armSealer` (new, optional, default `true`) and a function-valued `cryptoProvider`.
- An optional `seal` on `MailLogBodyMigrationOptions`, `KeyMaterialMigrationOptions` and the options of `migrateStoredMetadataBodyCopies`.
- `refused` on the three migration reports, total and per table in `byObject`.
- `sys_audit_amendment` registered and provisioned, with its labels in every locale bundle.
- `os migrate audit-metadata-bodies`, `audit-mail-bodies` and `audit-key-material`: the JSON report gains `refused`, and a run that refuses a row exits 1. No new flag and no new error code.
- `os migrate audit-metadata-bodies` keeps each row's stored `updated_at`, as its two siblings do.

No previously accepted call is refused. The package entry (`exports` has `.` alone) gains no new name: the writer, `SigningKeyTrust`, `anchoredPublicKeyOf` and `readAll` are reached by path inside the package and marked `@internal`. No state that exited 0 before exits 1 now, since no shipped host could seal a row before this PR.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Audit tamper-evidence is a security boundary. The admission rule is stated here at the rule level only.
- Not relaxed: no provider, an unopenable seed, a signer that cannot sign, a key-id mismatch, a failed amendment insert, a row that no longer matches its checkpoint, and a column sealed in clear each refuse the row. Every fault inside the decision reads as a refusal, never as a rewrite.
- #9863: the serve construction carries the host's own provider and the one-shot posture, and no config-derived option. The pin's other assertions are unchanged.
- Still owed before P4, unchanged from the previous record: the sealer/migration lock, the ruling on an app-supplied `AuditPlugin`, `@objectstack/verify`'s crypto-less `bootStack` plugin, and the stale `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['plugin-audit']` comment in `packages/spec`.
- PR author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` through the relay. The PR is a draft, mergeable and clean against `main`, with no auto-merge armed.

Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgVaKJ9TPfXPRhdqx3e`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`os serve` 把它封存所有密钥用的同一个加密提供者交给审计封存器；一次性命令（`os audit verify`、`os migrate …`）不再启动封存器；三条改写审计行的迁移在改写已封存的行之前先写一条签名的「脱敏修正记录」，写不了就拒绝改写并计数。
- 为什么改：此前没有宿主把加密提供者交给 AuditPlugin，声明了封存的对象封存不了；ADR-0154 D7 要求改写已封存行前先留签名记录，否则校验会把合法脱敏读成篡改。
- 风险与回滚：默认没有对象启用封存，现有部署行为不变；唯一可见变化是 `os migrate audit-metadata-bodies` 保留行原有的 `updated_at`。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/amendment-writer.ts`、`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mail-log-body-migration.ts`、`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/audit-seal/audit-seal-redaction-live.integration.test.ts`，预期 13 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地（已做完的非专题卡照常落地，见下）。
- 席位意见：同意落地。契约复审 PASS 6824178936（`150cac4b`），合 main 后的 delta PASS 在本 head；性能小问题已转跟进卡 #32737（挂 #31908 下）。#31908 留开，P4 仍在卡上。

- Head: `2c47c2856324541e38c8404ad41ad25b44d00b29` (GitHub's merge of `main` `cbf6956f`, no conflict resolution); 12 behind `main`, under the 15-commit merge bar.
- Shape: 52 files, +2533 / −142, Tier S (no governed path, under 3000 lines); `Part of #31908`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and the changeset.

- Accepted deviations: nits N1 and N3 of 6824178936. Out of scope: follow-up #32737 under #31908; the residuals the review routed privately went to the security seat, not here.
- Landing: the maintainer's word, verbatim 「已经做完的当然可以落地」「我说的 是后续只做专题卡」 (project "Objectstack security ui", project timeline, 2026-11-12): finished non-epic work still lands. `needs:contract-review` is removed with this landing.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [43249637278](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/43249637278) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/43249637278/job/131291920822)** — 失败步骤: Boot example apps and exercise real user flows

